Description DFRobot Terminal Block Board Designed for FireBeetle 2 ESP32-e IoT Microcontroller Features stable, reliable connections with terminal block wiring Includes LED status indicators for each terminal block Offers an external voltage input of 7-24 V and a GDI port The Terminal Block Board for FireBeetle 2 ESP32-e IoT Microcontroller is an expansion shield specifically designed to be compatible with the FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E IoT Microcontroller, supporting both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. However, it is important to note that it is not compatible with the FireBeetle 2 Board ESP32-S3 Microcontroller and Firebeetle 2 M0 Development Board. This expansion shield is ideally suited for those who prefer to use terminal blocks for wiring their projects. It is equipped with an additional 7-24V external voltage input and a GDI port. The use of terminal blocks ensures that wires are secured, resulting in more stable and reliable connections. Each terminal block, with the exception of GND, is fitted with an LED for status indication. A switch is incorporated into the design of the board, allowing users to turn off the LED when it is not needed. The terminal block board is characterized by its stable and reliable connections, with all pins of the mainboard broken out. The board also features an external Voltage Input of 7-24V, a GDI for connecting the display, a clear colorful silkscreen, a terminal block status indicator, and a terminal block status indicator switch. This makes it suitable for use in applications such as Smart Soil conditioners and Multiple Relays Projects. Please note that this expansion shield is not compatible with the FireBeetle 2 Board ESP32-S3 Microcontroller and Firebeetle 2 M0 Development Board. Description Compatible with products in the DFRobot FireBeetle serials Low-power consumption Quick Response(the top frequency is 400KHz) Small size, convenient to install The FireBeetle ESP32 IOT Microcontroller is the low-power consumption micro-controller intentionally designed for Internet of Things (IoT) projects. FireBeetle Board - ESP32 integrates a Dual-Core ESP-WROOM-32 module supports MCU and Wi-Fi and Bluetooth dual-mode communication. The electric current is just 10μA in the deep-sleep mode. The main controller supports two power supply methods: USB and 3.7V external lithium battery. And both USB and external DC can charge the Lipo battery directly. FireBeetle Board-ESP32 has made a special hardware design for Arduino IDE. You can make a download without switching booth-mode manually. Processer: Tensilica LX6 dual core processer (One for high speed connection; one for independent programing). Frequency: 240MHz SRAM：520KB Flash：16Mbit Wi-Fi standard：FCC/CE/TELEC/KCC Wi-Fi protocol: 802.11 b/g/n/d/e/I/k/r (802.11n, high speed can reach to 150 Mbps), converge A-MPDU and A-MSDU, supporting 0.4us protecting interval. Frequency range: 2.4~2.5 GHz Bluetooth protocol: Comply with BR/EDR/BLE standard of Bluetooth v4.2. Bluetooth audio: the current under low power consumption of CVSD and SBC is 10μA Working current: 80mA in average Frequency range: 2.4~2.5GHz Support one-key downloading. Support micropython. On-chip clock: 40MHz crystal and 32.768 KHz crystal. Digital I/O: 10 (default setting of arduino) Simulative input: 5(default setting of arduino) SPI: 1 (default setting of arduino) I2C: 1 (default setting of arduino) I2S: 1 (default setting of arduino) LED_BUILTIN：D9 Interface: FireBeetle series compatible Working temperature: -40℃~+85℃

Description FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3-U (N16R8) AIoT Microcontroller Board w/ Wi-Fi, Bluetooth & Camera Features high-performance ESP32-S3-U module Includes 2-megapixel OV2640 camera for image recognition Supports dual-mode communication with WiFi and Bluetooth 5 Designed with user-friendly onboard GDI screen interface The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3-U (N16R8) AIoT Microcontroller Board w/ Wi-Fi, Bluetooth & Camera is a high-performance primary controller, constructed around the ESP32-S3-U-WROOM-1-N16R8 module. This microcontroller comes with an OV2640 camera, making it highly suitable for applications that require image recognition. The ESP32-S3-U module is known for its generous storage capacity and a comprehensive set of communication interfaces, making it adaptable to a broad spectrum of application requirements. The included OV2640 camera, with its 2-megapixel capacity, a 68° field of view, and a resolution of up to 1600 x 1200, can be employed for home monitoring purposes. It can automatically send notifications and store image data when movement is detected. The ESP32-S3-U chip accelerates neural network computing and signal processing workloads, making the module a preferred choice for various applications, including speech and image recognition. The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3-U supports dual-mode communication with WiFi and Bluetooth 5 (LE), simplifying the networking process. It also supports Bluetooth Mesh protocol and Espressif WiFi Mesh, ensuring more stable communication and a larger coverage area. This development board is designed with user-friendliness in mind, addressing the intricacies of screen wiring through its onboard GDI screen interface. It also integrates power management features, including battery charging and hardware power control. The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3-U is compatible with programming through the Arduino IDE, ESP-IDF, and MicroPython, allowing developers to use both C and Python to interact with the hardware. The ESP32-S3 module is characterized by its substantial storage capacity and a comprehensive set of communication interfaces, making it adaptable to a broad spectrum of application requirements. It also supports both Bluetooth Mesh protocol and Espressif WiFi Mesh, ensuring more stable communication and a larger coverage area. This development board is designed with user-friendliness in mind, addressing the complexity of screen wiring through its onboard GDI screen interface. It also incorporates power management features, including battery charging and hardware power control. The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3 is compatible with the Arduino IDE, ESP-IDF, and MicroPython, allowing developers to use both C and Python to interact with the hardware.
